name: Hypopituitarism-Micropenis-Cleft Lip/Palate Syndrome
aliases: Hypopituitarism with Micropenis and Orofacial Clefting
Congenital Hypopituitarism with Cleft Lip and Palate

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Hypopituitarism-Micropenis-Cleft Lip/Palate Syndrome

criteria.description: Confirmed deficiency of one or more anterior pituitary hormones
Micropenis defined as stretched penile length below 2.5 standard deviations for age
Presence of cleft lip and/or cleft palate confirmed by clinical examination
MRI evidence of pituitary hypoplasia or structural abnormalities
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with pituitary development (e.g., HESX1, PROP1)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of hypopituitarism plus micropenis and cleft lip and/or palate
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires multidisciplinary evaluation including endocrinology, genetics, and craniofacial assessment.

laboratory: Low serum levels of pituitary hormones (GH, TSH, ACTH, LH, FSH, prolactin)
Low cortisol and thyroid hormone levels
imaging: MRI showing hypoplastic or absent anterior pituitary gland
Midline brain abnormalities such as absent septum pellucidum
Structural abnormalities of the sella turcica
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes involved in pituitary development (e.g., HESX1, PROP1, LHX4)
other: Clinical confirmation of cleft lip and/or palate by craniofacial specialist

distinguishingFeatures: Optic nerve hypoplasia with variable pituitary hormone deficiencies
Micropenis and hypogonadism without cleft lip/palate

redFlags: Neonatal hypoglycemia refractory to standard treatment
Failure to thrive with micropenis and midline facial defects
Severe respiratory distress due to cleft palate complications
